agenda_text:
AGENDA
HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  TUESDAY, January 7, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M.
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA CITY HALL
  CONFERENCE ROOM A
  111 S. FIRST ST.
  ALHAMBRA, CA 91801

1. ROLL CALL:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Mark Lee, Vice Chair
  Steven Cosci  Carolyn Ortiz
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan  Marc Tousignant
  Eric Sunada  Maria Conchita Bañuelos
  Marcos Sayon  Andrea Giese

2. INTRODUCTION – Introduction of new HCDA Committee Member.

3. MINUTES – Approval of the minutes for the Regular Meetings April 2, 2019, July 2, 2019
  and September 3, 2019.

4. PROGRESS REPORTS
  Attached for the Committee’s review are copies of the Progress Reports for those programs
  utilizing Community Development Block Grant and HOME Funds. All figures indicate the
  progress made and services rendered to date for FY 2019-2020.
   Parks and Recreation - Case Management
   90 Case Management clients were served.
   73 Volunteer Hours of assistance were donated to the program.
   Community Development - Code Enforcement
   The Code Enforcement Division investigated a total of 349 complaints.
   39 were identified as confirmed complaints as stand-alone Health & Safety Issues.
   Code Enforcement staff referred 105 to the Housing Department programs.
   Community Development - Fair Housing
   The Housing Rights Center served approx. 116 clients.
   A variety of issues were discussed, including: evictions, security deposits, rent
  increases, repairs, contract questions, etc.
   Community Development - Housing Programs
   First-Time Home Buyer - HOME: 9 searching for a home, 1 escrow closed.
   HOME Major Rehabilitation: 0 in process, 1 completed.
   CDBG Minor Rehabilitation: 0 in process, 1 completed.

  Recommended Action
  Receive and file these informational reports.

5. WORKING MEETING IN PREPARATION OF THE 2020-2024 CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND 2020-21 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN
  The City is required by the Department of Housing and Urban Development to prepare a
  “Consolidated Plan” and Annual Action Plans. The Consolidated Plan identifies the City’s
  programs funded with Housing and Urban Development Funds and the community’s needs
  over the next five years. This working meeting/discussion by the HCDA will focus on
  eligible CDBG and HOME activities and propose new or other funding recommendations
   under CDBG and HOME . Community organizations have been invited to participate in the
  meeting to give input on community development needs and fair housing issues in the City.
  Committee and public comments received will be considered as the City drafts its program
  plans for the 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan and the 2020-21 Annual Action Plan.
  Recommended Action
  Receive public comments and direct staff to include all comments received for consideration
  with the DRAFT 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan and 2020-21 Action Plan.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments must pertain
  to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee. Public comments pertaining to
  the HCDA Committee’s business are welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to five
  (5) minutes. Please complete the blue speaker card prior to the meeting and submit it to the
  Committee’s secretary.

7. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items
  discussed must pertain to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee.

8. ADJOURNMENT

 Copies of the staff report or other written documentation relating to each item of business described herein
 above are on file in the office of Management Services, Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra,
 CA, and are available for public inspection during regular office hours: 7:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M., Monday
 through Thursday.
 Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting described
 herein, he or she may contact Mr. Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst, either in person, at the
 Management Services Department located at City Hall, or call via telephone at (626) 570-5011, during
 regular business hours.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City meeting, please
 contact the City Clerk's Office (626) 570-5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will
 enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
minutes_text:
OFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of January 7, 2020
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

  Committee Chair Vallejos called the meeting to order at 7:00 pm.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Mark Lee, Vice Chair
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan  Carolyn Ortiz
  Eric Sunada  Steven Cosci
  Marcos Sayon  Maria Conchita Bañuelos
  Andrea Giese

  Committee Members Absent:
  Marc Tousignant

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst
  Veronica Tam, Principal, Veronica Tam and Associates

2. INTRODUCTION
  Committee Member Andrea Giese was introduced as the newest HCDA Committee
  Member.

3. MINUTES
  The Committee reviewed the minutes for the Regular Meetings of April 2, 2019; July 2, 2019
  and September 3, 2019.

  Committee Action:
  Committee Member Ortiz moved, seconded by Committee Member Sayon, to approve the
  minutes for the meetings of April 2, 2019, July 2, 2019 and September 3, 2019.
  Ayes:  Vallejos, Lee, Sharma-Ngan, Ortiz, Cosci, Sayon, Bañuelos, and Giese.
  Noes:  None.
  Abstain: Sunada.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  There was consensus from the Committee to hear comments from the audience at this
  point in the meeting.

  Grant Power, Habitat for Humanity of San Gabriel Valley, spoke about one of the
  organization’s objectives to obtain and rehabilitate properties to be set aside for low income
  families for long term housing needs. Mr. Power stated that Habitat for Humanity of San
  Gabriel Valley was looking forward to working with the City to achieve these goals.

  Susan Lin, Housing Rights Center, spoke about the recent rent stabilization law AB 1428 and
  its protections for renters. Ms. Lin also suggested additional coordination with the City on
  public outreach efforts to inform renters of their rights under the new law.
  Page 1 of 4
 4. PROGRESS REPORTS
  The Committee reviewed the reports. Assistant City Manager Garcia provided a brief update
  in regards to the change in the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
  reporting requirements for Code Enforcement. All figures indicate the progress made and
  services rendered to the date for Fiscal Year 2019/2020.

  Committee Action:
  The Committee received and filed these informational reports.

5. WORKING MEETING IN PREPARATION OF THE 2020-2024 CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND 2020-21 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN
  Assistant City Manager Garcia provided a brief update regarding a recent audit conducted by
  HUD. Assistant City Manager Garcia stated HUD identified one finding, and the City
  implemented new procedures to address this concern and submitted its corrections to HUD.

  Committee Member Sunada stated he felt the full Committee could not move forward tonight
  because it lacked proper training and clear understanding of the Committee’s role.
  Committee Member Sunada stated that the Committee has not been given the necessary
  training as requested. He also spoke about the Committee not meeting regularly and recent
  meeting cancellations were not per the Committee’s prerogative but done by staff, and the
  lack of meetings did not allow for the Committee to complete its year-end report.
  Committee Member Sunada felt the municipal code provided more context and authority to
  the Committee in selecting a Committee Secretary and setting meeting dates and agendas.

  Committee Chair Vallejos indicated this was not the appropriate portion of the agenda to
  discuss these issues and that the Committee needs to focus on the current agenda item.

  Veronica Tam, Veronica Tam and Associates, provided a presentation on the City’s HUD
  funds. The presentation included background information and eligible uses for the CDBG
  and HOME programs as well as funding allocations for each program. Ms. Tam also
  reiterated the Committee’s goal tonight was to provide recommendations to City Council for
  future allocations.

  Various questions were asked by Committee Members regarding the City’s HUD funds.
  • Number of properties acquired and rehabilitated by the City.
  • The current amount of banked funds.
  • Budget totals and what happens to unexpended funds for each program.
  • Additional eligible uses for HUD funds.
  • Allocations for Administrative functions and minimum amounts that can be
  designated.

  Committee Chair Vallejos stated that each Committee Member would be given five minutes
  to provide their recommended allocations and priorities, and any other additional comments
  or suggestions on how to allocate future funding for the upcoming five-year period.

  Committee Member Cosci provided his proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for Housing
  Rehabilitation, Code Enforcement, Public Facilities, and Street/Infrastructure.

  Page 2 of 4
   Committee Member Bañuelos provided her proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period with an emphasis on public facility
  improvements in particular for City parks.

  Committee Member Sayon provided his proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for public
  facilities, housing rehabilitation, crime prevention and administration.

  Committee Member Ortiz provided her proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for housing
  rehabilitation, public facilities, energy efficiency, code enforcement and administration.

  Committee Member Giese provided her proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for housing
  rehabilitation, case management, code enforcement and public facilities.

  Committee Member Sunada reiterated previous comments that the Committee needed more
  time to analyze and allocate funding for the five-year plan and was not going to give his
  recommended allocations. Committee Members Sunada felt the Committee needed to be
  more strategic in its approach and look to County and State resources to leverage more funds.

  Committee Member Lee stated he needed additional time to further analyze the data as
  presented; however, he indicated that higher prioritization should be given to energy
  efficiency and crime prevention for the upcoming five-year period.

  Committee Member Sharma-Ngan provided her proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG
  and HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for housing
  rehabilitation, youth and childcare, case management, energy efficiency, and public facilities.

  Committee Chair Vallejos provided his proposed allocations for the City’s CDBG and
  HOME programs for the upcoming five-year period including prioritization for youth and
  childcare, crisis housing, public facilities, and minimum funding for administration.
  Committee Chair Vallejos also stated the City should move away from the first-time home
  buyer program, and the Committee should acquire more knowledge on how CDBG and
  HOME programs work.

  Committee Action:
  There was consensus among the Committee that additional time was needed to analyze the
  information presented and return at a future meeting to vote on specific future recommended
  funding allocation amounts.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  Committee Chair Vallejos opened the meeting up to additional comments from the audience.

  Susan Lin, Housing Rights Center, provided clarification on the specific services the Housing
  Rights Center provides. Ms. Lin also spoke about many clients in need of rental assistance
  and code enforcement issues at rental properties. She stated many of her clients have
  contacted City code enforcement and that Code Enforcement was not assisting them
  regarding their complaints. Ms. Lin stated she felt there needs to be more follow up regarding
  these issues and what actions code enforcement can take to address them.

  Page 3 of 4
 7. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Committee Member Ortiz requested if the Committee could be provided charts comparing
  the various programs and amounts allocated over the years to help determine if funds were
  being spent efficiently. She felt charts would assist current and future Committee Members in
  regards to where future allocations should be dedicated.

  Committee Member Sunada restated prior comments pertaining to the lack of training and
  the Committee being prevented from meeting on a regular basis which prohibits continuity.
  He again commented that the Committee should be allowed to set its own agenda and select a
  Committee Secretary.

  The Committee had further discussion on additional training and were in agreement that
  additional training and information on CDBG and HOME programs was needed.

8. ADJOURNMENT: 9:09 p.m.
